clue.text: One work unit's about to be in line for delicate metalwork

parts.note: first part of FILE, a line or row, opened up to take the insert
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the work unit is read from its end back to its start
to be in something is to sit inside it, so the preceding letters go inside the word for line

parts.note: the erg is the unit of work in physics
last letter of FILE, closing round the insert

explanation.surface: A worker is about to join the queue for a piece of fine jewellery-making.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus ERG turned round makes IGRE, which sits inside FILE (a line, as in single file).
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is ornamental work made from fine twisted threads of gold or silver wire.

clue.text: Fit for party leader? The leader has been deposed

indicators.note: the leader being deposed means the first letter of the politician's name is removed

parts.note: William Hague led the Conservative Party when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone is fit to lead a party, followed by news of a toppled leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective (suitable), but it is a noun: a bout of illness. Hague was Tory leader 1997-2001.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fever with recurring shivering bouts, so a fit or attack of illness.

clue.text: See 18
Comic cut short: time's up for comic character

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its final letter off

parts.note: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A comic is cancelled early, and time is up for one of its characters.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Comic' is the Dandy, losing its Y; the second sits in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan Dare, pilot of the future, was the space-hero star of the British Eagle comic from 1950.

clue.text: Move the old books I'm mad about?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the words before it are placed around the books

parts.note: LOCO (mad) with ME standing in for I, read as 'me loco'
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are crazy enough to shift a heap of ancient books.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCO and ME open between the M and E to admit OT.
explanation.definitionFit: To locomote is to travel or progress from place to place, a formal word for moving about.

clue.text: Home Secretary and rock'n'roll guitarist: one's barren, another's wild

parts.note: Jack Straw was Home Secretary from 1997 to 2001
Chuck Berry, the rock'n'roll guitarist

explanation.surface: A politician and a rock star are compared: one is unfruitful, the other untamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: the barren strawberry and the wild strawberry are both plants named after the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren strawberry and wild strawberry are names of two plant species, so this fruit-plant has both kinds.

clue.text: Make one's home in Cumbrian town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take up residence somewhere
second meaning: a market town in the Yorkshire Dales

explanation.surface: Someone moves house to a small town in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is in fact in North Yorkshire, near the Cumbrian border, at the start of the Settle-Carlisle railway into Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to establish a permanent residence; Settle is also a northern English market town.

clue.text: Wade, perhaps in Surrey water

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first name of Wade, the British tennis player who won Wimbledon in 1977
second meaning: the word that comes before Water in the name of a Surrey village beside a lake

explanation.surface: Someone wades into a stretch of water in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wade' looks like a verb about paddling, but it is a surname; the second half is a name with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is Wade's first name, and Virginia Water is a Surrey place with a lake, so both senses fit.

clue.text: See 18
See 26
One day TV is to be free of offensive recording

indicators.note: setting the words free lets their letters loose to fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hope that one day television will be rid of offensive content.
explanation.definitionFit: Video nasty was the 1980s British tabloid term for violent or obscene horror films on videocassette.

clue.text: See 25
Aussie flier twice took gold, overhauling silver both times

parts.note: taking gold means winning

indicators.note: overhauling here means turning over, so the word for silver is flipped round

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the win comes round a second time
the silver is turned over again on the repeat

explanation.surface: An Australian athlete won gold twice, beating the silver medallist on both occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like an athlete or pilot, but it is a bird. WON plus reversed AG, done 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wonga-wonga is a large Australian pigeon, so a bird native to Australia.

clue.text: Spooner has to offer a kick up the backside to get a drink in North America

indicators.note: Spooner, the clergyman famous for swapping word beginnings, signals that opening sounds are exchanged

parts.words: to offer a kick up the backside
parts.note: to boot someone's rear is to kick their backside; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: Spooner is ready to kick someone in the backside to get a drink while in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras, popular in the USA and Canada.

clue.text: Home of the meadow pipit, perhaps, most inadequate

wordplay.words: Home of the meadow pipit, perhaps
wordplay.note: a meadow pipit could make its nest in a lea, a poetic word for meadow: LEA plus NEST

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note on where the meadow pipit lives, oddly tagged as poorest.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA is an old word for a meadow; a bird's home is its NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean means meagre or scanty, so leanest is the most meagre or insufficient.

clue.text: Shearer's possession, the overhead kick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cutting tool someone who shears would own
second meaning: the acrobatic football kick taken in mid-air

explanation.surface: Footballer Alan Shearer has the ball and attempts a bicycle kick.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer was England's centre-forward, so 'Shearer's possession' sounds like football; here a shearer is someone cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissors are a two-bladed cutting tool, and a scissors kick is a football volley struck overhead.

clue.text: Cumbrian town in H. Pinter play

indicators.note: to play with something is to move its parts about freely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern town hosts a Harold Pinter drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a Pinter drama, but it tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Penrith is a market town in Cumbria, in north-west England near the Lake District.

clue.text: Ken Livingstone and the FT go h-h-horribly together for a culling of Tory ministers

indicators.note: horribly means in a dreadful, mangled way, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the two stammered letters count too

explanation.surface: London's mayor and the Financial Times make an unlikely pair in some stuttering political drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer's extra H's are part of the fodder. Ken Livingstone was London's mayor; the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan's sacking of seven Cabinet colleagues in 1962 was nicknamed after Hitler's 1934 purge of rivals.

clue.text: Bond once by following Buddhism south of Los Angeles

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word by is placed behind the Buddhist school

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles
Zen is a school of Buddhism
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former 007 took up Buddhism after moving to Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'south of' means placed below, so Los Angeles sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lazenby played James Bond once, in On Her Majesty's Secret Service (1969).

clue.text: Extinct bird with nails hammered in — work of Enigmatist?

indicators.note: the bird holds the other letters within it
in shows the battered letters go inside the bird

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so the letters are bashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone nails up a stuffed dodo-like bird as a piece of art by a puzzle setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigmatist is a fellow Guardian setter's pseudonym, but here it means the painter of the most enigmatic smile, Leonardo.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is famous for its sitter's enigmatic smile, so it is the masterpiece of an enigma-maker.

clue.text: Drug given for nothing? Then one's head going round

parts.note: zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the head wraps round the single letter

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drug handed out free, and then the user's head starts spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: I sits inside PATE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic drug derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Poet's boring to study

parts.note: something dry is dull and boring
a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: A poet is dull to study at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb, but it is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the 17th-century English poet laureate, author of Absalom and Achitophel.

clue.text: Plane providing information about fighter's downfall

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the information is placed round the downfall

parts.note: data is information
a knockout, KO, is a boxer's downfall

explanation.surface: An aircraft supplies intelligence on how a fighter plane was shot down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a warplane beside 'Plane', but it is a boxer, whose downfall is a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas Dakota was the RAF name for the DC-3 transport aircraft of World War II.

clue.text: Spider, if black, say, a feature of Dracula?

parts.note: the black widow is a venomous spider
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: A note on spiders: if it is black, perhaps it is a mark of a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read WIDOW SPEAK, which is respaced as WIDOW'S PEAK. 'Say' looks like 'for example' but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow's peak is a V-shaped point of hair on the forehead, classically drawn on screen vampires.

clue.text: Railway from Birmingham reportedly to be cut

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, here in a Brummie accent

parts.note: a railway is a line, which in a Birmingham accent comes out with an 'oi' vowel

explanation.surface: A rail service out of Birmingham is to be axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the verb to axe, but it is a cut of meat. The Brummie accent turns long I into OI.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a cut of meat taken from the back between ribs and hips, such as pork loin.

clue.text: See 18
Crustaceans in spring water all at sea

indicators.note: being all at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shellfish found in spring water, which are completely out of place there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' fits the crustaceans in the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger prawns are large striped prawns, a kind of crustacean eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Mistress got her teeth into the Arsenal?

parts.note: bit on means bit into something
taken as written
Arsenal is a London football side

explanation.surface: A woman sinks her teeth into the Arsenal team, maybe as a fierce fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistress' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is British slang for a secret lover taken outside one's marriage.
